newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says maintains Tesco's ratings. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IBCA says maintains Tesco's ratings. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]

text.p: Rating agency IBCA said on Thursday it maintained the ratings of Tesco Plc at AA minus (corrects from AA) long term and A1 plus short term.
"The ratings reflect Tesco's strong market position in UK food retailing and consistently sound financial profile", the rating agency said in a statement.

IBCA said Tesco has outperformed the British market in the past 18 months and has overtaken J Sainsbury to rank as Britain's leading food retailer, with a market share estimated at around 13.6 percent.
The agency said the company had faced intense competition, a tight planning environment and price pressure amongst the major food retailers.

It said Tesco had responded with the introduction of a differentiated store portfolio, the targeted use of price promotions and campaigns, and the launch of an innovative customer loyalty scheme and selective geographical expansion.

IBCA said Tesco's overseas expansion into France and central Europe still remains small in group terms although operations may provide a base from which future expansion can be driven to counter the slowing of growth in the domestic sector.

"Nonetheless, despite fears of the possible escalation of an autumn 1996 price war amongst the UK majors, the strength of earnings and cash flow from the core UK operations and the solidity of financial coverage measures underpin the current ratings," the agency said.
